proposal.title: Campaign timeline — AION shifts major software development to 32-bit Artemis
proposal.reason: Convert this campaign to an independent dated timeline object. Dates are resolved from its execution process without changing precision. Preserve all existing event/subprocess ownership; marketing-step reference_id is absent throughout. Consolidate presentations, campaign material and useful claim-policy requirements into narrated steps; remove historical acceptance labels and duplicate import fragments. Product-owned launch links remain authoritative and validated through the explicit transitional execution mapping. Add the campaign alongside the unchanged execution-process step in process.native_abacus_pulse_development.

before.title: AION shifts major software development to 32-bit Artemis
before.objective: Promote the forthcoming Abacus 3 and Pulse 3 offerings on Artemis through pre-show advertising and qualified business-workflow demonstrations at COMDEX on 19 November 1980, and introduce the Budget Hard-Disk Office package at the same event.

marketing_content.description: Beginning 19 October 1980, use trade-press advertising and dealer/customer invitations to promote the COMDEX presentation of native Abacus 3 and Pulse 3. Keep announcement and released availability distinct.

Prepare business examples using formatted tables, graphical reporting and repeatable Pulse automation on Artemis. State tested RAM, disk, correctness and recovery limits, report compatibility progress and retain Aurelia/Aurelia+ maintenance messaging.

Introduce Artemis Budget Hard-Disk Office at COMDEX on 19 November 1980 with its 5 MB hard disk. Abacus 3 is separately selectable at launch. Demonstrations must use qualified configurations; networking remains a later option.

before.title: 32-bit Native Abacus/Pulse development
before.description: Develop and qualify native Abacus 3.0 and Pulse 3.0 for 32-bit Artemis from 14 February to 21 December 1980. Present the resulting applications through the COMDEX 1980 campaign while maintaining the existing Aurelia/Aurelia+ software line.

inputs.description: The earlier AIONix architecture and portability work establishes the operating-system direction for native Artemis software.
Existing Abacus and Pulse implementations provide the application lineage and behaviour to preserve in the native editions.

Implement against the AIONix interfaces and Artemis resource constraints; target integration and qualification occur as suitable builds and hardware become available during the development period. This does not require released hardware at the start of exploratory work.

steps.description: Implement native Abacus 3.0 and Pulse 3.0 for Artemis, including formatted tables, bounded columnar storage, calculated columns and lookups, read-only SQL queries, graphical reporting, embedded Pulse and supported logical-record imports.
Qualify RAM and disk use, arithmetic and query correctness, recovery and execution times using repeatable business workflows; do not promise unlimited datasets or guaranteed compression.
Present the native products and demonstrated business workflows through the COMDEX 1980 campaign, retaining the existing launch milestone.
Complete the development period with documented supported configurations and reviewed demonstration feedback while preserving maintenance and simplified refreshes for Aurelia/Aurelia+.

outcomes.description: Native Abacus 3.0 and Pulse 3.0 form the Artemis-focused application generation presented at COMDEX, with documented resource limits and qualified business workflows.

The native application generation implements formatted tables and embedded Pulse integration in Abacus, covering bounded columnar storage, calculated columns and lookups, read-only SQL queries and graphical reporting within documented resource limits.
